To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a planet has been discovered in the microlens event MOA-2012-BLG-505.

a Jupiter mass planet has been discovered orbiting a star in the range 7-80% of the mass of the sun, at a distance of 1.5-3 AU, and a period of 3.8-8 years, in a direction toward the Galactic bulge, at a distance in the range 3-8 kpc.

the microlensing planet MOA-2007-BLG-192Lb has a high planet-to-host mass ratio of q = 0 0132 ± 003 and that the planet orbits an M dwarf at a projected separation of a = 1.5 AU with an orbital period P = 4.7 yr.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the formation, evolution, and structure of the interstellar medium (ISM), and the role it plays in star and planet formation.
the study of the structure, dynamics and evolution of the Galaxy.
the formation of planetary systems and the search for planets outside our own solar system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have discovered a massive planet orbiting a low-mass M dwarf.
the planet has a mass of 3.3 ± 0.6 M_J, and is orbiting a metal-poor (about [Fe/H] = -0.5) M-dwarf host at an estimated distance of 5.8 kpc.
the microlensing planet MOA-2007-BLG- 387Lb is an Saturn-mass planet orbiting an early M-dwarf at a semimajor axis of 1.5 AU, but with a significant range of possibilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we find a massive planet orbiting a low-mass M dwarf at a distance between the orbits of Saturn and Uranus.
we have discovered a Jupiter-mass planet orbiting a 0.2 M_⊙ host at 1.5 AU, which is well into the habitable zone of the star.
we have discovered a Jupiter mass planet orbiting an early M-dwarf at a distance of 5 kpc with a period of 5 years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the host is likely to be an M dwarf.
the microlensing planetary signal is so well-measured that in the presence of a fairly general prior, the low-mass end of the host star mass function is firmly excluded.
the microlens parallaxes of planets are highly correlated with the planet mass ratio and thus the planet mass.
